angle: Unlike other L09 materials that derive intervals or debate bias, this under-three-minute quickie reduces the standard-deviation-versus-standard-error distinction to a single image of five mice weighed once versus five repeated means.
angle_detail: Watch [00:52]–[01:40] first, where five repeated experiments produce five means whose spread is named the standard error. Then take [01:40]–[02:10] as the exam rule: deviation describes one measured sample, error describes means across repeats. Remember the pitfall flagged at [02:03]: the error can be estimated from a single sample even though it describes many, so plot the deviation for measured data and skip the onward pointers from [02:31].
